title: Accept Slices Instead of Vectors
goal: Learn why public function signatures should take slice references rather than vector references.

sections.text: In Go or Java, passing a slice or list reference is standard. In Rust, functions that only read items should accept `&[T]` instead of `&Vec<T>`.

sections.caption: A slice parameter accepts vectors, arrays, and slices.

sections.text: A `&Vec<T>` parameter restricts your callers. Callers with fixed arrays `[T; N]` or slice views cannot call your function without creating a new `Vec`.
Through deref coercion, a `&Vec<T>` automatically converts into `&[T]`. Passing `&[T]` gives your API maximum caller flexibility at zero performance cost.

sections.caption: Both vector references and fixed arrays fit the same parameter.

sections.text: Generics like `AsRef` extend this idea further, which is covered in the trait bounds deck later.

explanation: Learn why public function signatures should take slice references rather than vector references.
